dedupe_keys.name: sto cast spatiotemporal outage forecast deep learning model for tropical cyclone power outages 4 km hourly typhoon muifa case

description: STO-CAST, the SpatioTemporal Outage ForeCAST model, is a deep learning framework for real-time, regional-scale prediction of power outages during tropical cyclones, described in a December 2025 arXiv preprint marked as under review. It integrates static environmental and infrastructure attributes with dynamic meteorological and outage sequences using gated recurrent units and fully connected layers, and is trained with a Leave-One-Storm-Out cross-validation strategy plus holdout grid experiments to show preliminary generalisation to unseen storms and grids. The model produces hourly outage forecasts at 4 km by 4 km resolution in two modes, short-term nowcasting with a 6-hour lead time by assimilating real-time observations and long-term forecasting with a 60-hour lead time from evolving meteorological projections. A case study on Typhoon Muifa (2022) demonstrates operational effectiveness, including error decomposition across model design, meteorological uncertainty and observation gaps. Access: the paper on arXiv, free; no code or licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: preprint under review, and the outage data source is not identified in the abstract. It suits outage forecasting and emergency response planning for cyclone-exposed grids, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
